subproblems.title: Injective-immersion area formula on a Borel subset of ℝ^m with Gram-determinant Jacobian
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, and let F ⊆ ℝ^m be a Borel set. Assume G is differentiable at every v ∈ F with injective derivative DG(v), and G is injective on F. Let e_0, …, e_{m−1} be the standard basis of ℝ^m.

Then for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ:
∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j<m})^{1/2} · h(G(v)) dL^m(v).

Here H^m = μHE[m] is the normalized m-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and L^m is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m. Both sides are Bochner integrals; no integrability is assumed, and a non-integrable integral is 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (G : Euclid m → Euclid P) (F : Set (Euclid m)), MeasurableSet F → (∀ v ∈ F, DifferentiableAt ℝ G v) → (∀ v ∈ F, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G v)) → InjOn G F → ∀ h : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ w in G '' F, h w ∂μHE[m] = ∫ v in F, Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))) * h (G v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This is the comparator-accepted DAG theorem Submission.codim1_lur_cd_injective_area_formula_gram (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.local_unit_rep-a1.chart_divergence-a1.gram_area_formula-a1).
- Accepted candidate: 15f8046553cb9af46b3f645a487e52fb756a62ac; its isolated comparator passed.
- Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
- Its Lean proof adds no import to the frozen header.
It is reused here with the identical frozen Lean type; no new formalization is requested.

Mathematical proof. Source: steps 5–6 of the supplied cone_area proof, stated for an arbitrary dimension m, map G and Borel set F (Simon Ch. 2, (3.3)–(3.5)).

1. (Area formula.) Apply the pinned SimonGMT theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean) with source space E = ℝ^m, target ℝ^P, s = F (measurable), f = G and g = h. Its hypotheses are exactly ours: G is differentiable at each point of F with injective derivative, and G is injective on F. It gives
∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v • h(G v) dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^m](v)
for every h : ℝ^P → ℝ, with no integrability hypothesis.
In the library this comes from the measure identity (G|_F)_*(J·μHE⌞F) = μHE⌞G(F), where J = areaJacobianAt G, using MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and setIntegral_withDensity_eq_setIntegral_smul₀. Here G|_F is a measurable embedding because G is continuous and injective on the Borel set F.

2. (Normalization.) finrank ℝ ℝ^m = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), and on ℝ^m, μHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^m] equals Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence
∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G v) dv.

3. (Gram form of the Jacobian.) Fix v ∈ F and put L := DG(v).
- By definition areaJacobianAt G v = normDet(L) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), and normDet(L) ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg).
- Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, applied to L and the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin m) ℝ (vectors e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1), gives normDet(L)² = det Gram(Le_0, …, Le_{m−1}) = det[⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩]_{i,j}.
- Taking the nonnegative square root (Real.sqrt_sq): areaJacobianAt G v = (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j})^{1/2}.

4. (Conclusion.) Substitute step 3 pointwise on the measurable set F into the right side of step 2 (setIntegral_congr_fun; the scalar action is real multiplication). This gives
∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩])^{1/2} · h(G(v)) dv. ∎

Remark. The accepted Lean proof reaches the same identity without the SimonGMT import:
1. Linear case: an injective linear B factors as an isometry onto its range composed with C : ℝ^m → ℝ^m, so Hᵐ(B S) = |det C| Lᵐ(S) and √det Gram(B) = |det C|.
2. A Lipschitz comparison of Hᵐ-images.
3. A partition of F into countably many measurable pieces on which G approximates injective linear maps (exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt), with an a.e. estimate on the derivative at density points.
4. Summation over the pieces, using Lusin–Souslin measurability of the images, then letting η → 0.
proof_key_steps: SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (E = ℝ^m, s = F, f = G, g = h): ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G · h∘G dμHE for every h, with no integrability hypothesis.
On ℝ^m, finrank = m and μHE[m] = volume.

areaJacobianAt G v = normDet DG(v) ≥ 0, and normDet² = det Gram(DG(v)e_i) for the standard orthonormal basis (normDet_sq_eq_det_gram). So areaJacobianAt = √(det Gram); conclude with setIntegral_congr_fun on F.

subproblems.title: The cone parametrization (t, α) ↦ tγ(α) is an injective immersion on the box
subproblems.statement:
Let P ∈ ℕ and r₀, s ∈ ℝ with 0 < s < r₀. Let γ : ℝ → ℝ^P be C¹ and injective on I := (−s, s), and for every α ∈ I assume ‖γ(α)‖ = 1, ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 0 and γ′(α) ≠ 0, where γ′ = deriv γ. Put R := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s) × I ⊆ ℝ × ℝ and G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^P, G(t, α) := tγ(α).

Then G is injective on R. Moreover, for every z = (t, α) ∈ R, G is (Fréchet) differentiable at z, its derivative DG(z) : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^P is injective, DG(z)(1, 0) = γ(α) and DG(z)(0, 1) = tγ′(α).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (r₀ s : ℝ) (γ : ℝ → Euclid P), 0 < s → s < r₀ → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Ioo (-s) s) → InjOn γ (Ioo (-s) s) → (∀ α ∈ Ioo (-s) s, ‖γ α‖ = 1 ∧ inner ℝ (γ α) (deriv γ α) = 0 ∧ deriv γ α ≠ 0) → InjOn (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) (Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ×ˢ Ioo (-s) s) ∧ ∀ z ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ×ˢ Ioo (-s) s, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) z ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) z) ∧ fderiv ℝ (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) z (1, 0) = γ z.2 ∧ fderiv ℝ (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) z (0, 1) = z.1 • deriv γ z.2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the supplied cone_area proof (differentiability, injective derivative and injectivity of G(t, α) = tγ(α)), carried out directly on ℝ × ℝ.
Notation: J := (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), I := (−s, s), R := J × I, G(q) := q.1·γ(q.2) for q ∈ ℝ × ℝ, γ′ := deriv γ.

1. (Positivity.) If (t, α) ∈ R then t > r₀ − s > 0, because s < r₀.

2. (G is injective on R.) Let (t, α), (t′, α′) ∈ R with tγ(α) = t′γ(α′).
- Take norms. Using ‖cv‖ = |c|‖v‖, ‖γ(α)‖ = ‖γ(α′)‖ = 1 and t, t′ > 0 (step 1) gives t = t′.
- Then tγ(α) = tγ(α′) with t ≠ 0 gives γ(α) = γ(α′), by cancelling a nonzero scalar in a real vector space.
- Injectivity of γ on I gives α = α′.
Hence (t, α) = (t′, α′).

3. (γ is differentiable on I.) Let α ∈ I. Since γ is C¹ on I, it is differentiable on I (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with 1 ≤ 1). I is open and contains α, so it is a neighbourhood of α and γ is differentiable at α. Thus γ has derivative γ′(α) at α (HasDerivAt γ (γ′(α)) α).

4. (Derivative of G.) Fix z = (t, α) ∈ R.
- The first projection π₁(q) = q.1 has derivative fst : (a, b) ↦ a.
- By the chain rule, γ ∘ π₂ (with π₂(q) = q.2) has derivative L₂ : (a, b) ↦ b·γ′(α) at z. Here the derivative of γ at α, viewed as a continuous linear map ℝ → ℝ^P, is c ↦ c·γ′(α), and it is composed with snd.
- By the product rule for a scalar function times a vector function (HasFDerivAt.smul), G = π₁·(γ ∘ π₂) has derivative L := t·L₂ + fst(·)·γ(α) at z, i.e. L(a, b) = t b γ′(α) + a γ(α).
Therefore G is differentiable at z and DG(z) = fderiv ℝ G z = L (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).

5. (Coordinate values.)
- L(1, 0) = t·0·γ′(α) + 1·γ(α) = γ(α) = γ(z.2).
- L(0, 1) = t·1·γ′(α) + 0·γ(α) = tγ′(α) = z.1·γ′(z.2).

6. (DG(z) is injective.) L is linear, so it suffices to show that L(a, b) = 0 implies (a, b) = (0, 0). Suppose t b γ′(α) + a γ(α) = 0.
- Take the inner product with γ(α). Since ⟨γ(α), γ′(α)⟩ = 0 and ⟨γ(α), γ(α)⟩ = ‖γ(α)‖² = 1, this gives t b·0 + a·1 = 0, so a = 0.
- Then (t b)γ′(α) = 0 with γ′(α) ≠ 0 gives t b = 0, and t > 0 (step 1) gives b = 0.

7. (Conclusion.) Step 2 shows G is injective on R. Steps 4–6 show that for every z ∈ R, G is differentiable at z, DG(z) is injective, DG(z)(1, 0) = γ(z.2) and DG(z)(0, 1) = z.1·γ′(z.2). The hypothesis 0 < s is not used. ∎

Formalization notes. A complete Lean proof of this exact type compiles from `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` alone, with axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
- Structure: intro the hypotheses and split with refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩.
- InjOn: rintro ⟨t, α⟩ ⟨ht, hα⟩ ⟨t', α'⟩ ⟨ht', hα'⟩ heq. Rewrite congrArg norm heq with norm_smul, the unit-norm hypotheses, Real.norm_eq_abs and abs_of_pos to get t = t' (subst). Then smul_right_injective _ htpos.ne' heq gives γ α = γ α'; finish with hinj.
- Derivative of γ: hdγ : HasDerivAt γ (deriv γ α) α := ((hγ.differentiableOn (by norm_num)).differentiableAt (Ioo_mem_nhds hα.1 hα.2)).hasDerivAt.
- State the two factors with explicit types:
  h1 : HasFDerivAt (Prod.fst : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ) (ContinuousLinearMap.fst ℝ ℝ ℝ) (t, α) := hasFDerivAt_fst
  h2 : HasFDerivAt (γ ∘ Prod.snd) ((ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight (1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ) (deriv γ α)).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.snd ℝ ℝ ℝ)) (t, α) := hdγ.hasFDerivAt.comp (t, α) hasFDerivAt_snd
- Then hD : HasFDerivAt (fun q : ℝ × ℝ => q.1 • γ q.2) (t • ((ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight (1 : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ) (deriv γ α)).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.snd ℝ ℝ ℝ)) + (ContinuousLinearMap.fst ℝ ℝ ℝ).smulRight (γ α)) (t, α) := h1.smul h2.
- Pitfalls: HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt applies only to scalar-valued outer maps, and writing hasFDerivAt_fst.smul … inline fails higher-order unification.
- After rw [hD.fderiv], the two coordinate values close by simp.
- Injectivity: rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]; rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab; simp only [add_apply, smul_apply, comp_apply, smulRight_apply, coe_fst', coe_snd', one_apply] at hab. Apply congrArg (fun v => inner ℝ (γ α) v) and simp with inner_add_right, real_inner_smul_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq and the hypotheses to get a = 0. Then smul_eq_zero and mul_eq_zero give b = 0.
proof_key_steps: For (t, α) ∈ R, t > r₀ − s > 0.
If tγ(α) = t′γ(α′): taking norms (‖γ‖ = 1) gives t = t′; cancelling t gives γ(α) = γ(α′); injectivity of γ on I gives α = α′.
γ is differentiable at α ∈ I because it is C¹ on the open interval.
Product and chain rules give DG(t, α)(a, b) = aγ(α) + tbγ′(α), so DG(1, 0) = γ(α) and DG(0, 1) = tγ′(α).
DG is injective: pairing with γ(α) (γ ⊥ γ′, ‖γ‖ = 1) forces a = 0; then tbγ′(α) = 0 with γ′(α) ≠ 0 and t > 0 forces b = 0.

subproblems.title: Area formula for an injective immersion of a measurable subset of ℝ × ℝ into ℝ^P
subproblems.statement:
Let P ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^P, and let R ⊆ ℝ × ℝ be measurable. Assume G is differentiable at every q ∈ R with injective derivative DG(q) : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^P, and G is injective on R. Write ∂₁G(q) := DG(q)(1, 0) and ∂₂G(q) := DG(q)(0, 1).

Then for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ:
∫_{G(R)} h dH² = ∫_R (‖∂₁G(q)‖²‖∂₂G(q)‖² − ⟨∂₁G(q), ∂₂G(q)⟩²)^{1/2} · h(G(q)) dq.

Here H² = μHE[2] on ℝ^P and dq is the product Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ × ℝ. Both sides are Bochner integrals; no integrability is assumed.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (G : ℝ × ℝ → Euclid P) (R : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) (h : Euclid P → ℝ), MeasurableSet R → (∀ q ∈ R, DifferentiableAt ℝ G q) → (∀ q ∈ R, Injective (fderiv ℝ G q)) → InjOn G R → ∫ x in G '' R, h x ∂μHE[2] = ∫ q in R, Real.sqrt (‖fderiv ℝ G q (1, 0)‖ ^ 2 * ‖fderiv ℝ G q (0, 1)‖ ^ 2 - inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ G q (1, 0)) (fderiv ℝ G q (0, 1)) ^ 2) * h (G q)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 5, 6 and 7 of the supplied cone_area proof (transport ℝ × ℝ ↔ Euclid 2, area formula, Gram determinant of two vectors, transport back), stated for a general injective immersion G of a measurable R ⊆ ℝ × ℝ. The area formula itself is the sibling gram_area (Submission.codim1_lur_cd_injective_area_formula_gram) with m = 2.
Notation: E₂ := Euclid 2; for w ∈ E₂, w₀ := w 0 and w₁ := w 1; e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 and e₁ := EuclideanSpace.single 1 1.

1. (Coordinate isomorphism.) Let e : E₂ → ℝ × ℝ, e(w) := (w₀, w₁). It is realized as the continuous linear equivalence (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin 2) ℝ).trans (ContinuousLinearEquiv.finTwoArrow ℝ ℝ), so e w = (w 0, w 1) holds definitionally. e is bijective, linear and continuous, and e(e₀) = (1, 0), e(e₁) = (0, 1).

2. (e preserves Lebesgue measure.) As a function, e = finTwoArrow ∘ (toLp 2)⁻¹. Composing EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp (Fin 2) with volume_preserving_finTwoArrow ℝ shows that e is measure preserving from volume on E₂ to volume (the product Lebesgue measure) on ℝ × ℝ. Being a homeomorphism, e is a measurable embedding.

3. (Pull back to E₂.) Let G̃ := G ∘ e : E₂ → ℝ^P and F := e⁻¹(R). F is measurable, since e is continuous and R is measurable.
- Chain rule for a continuous linear equivalence (ContinuousLinearEquiv.comp_right_fderiv): DG̃(w) = DG(e w) ∘ e for every w ∈ E₂, with no differentiability assumption.
- For w ∈ F we have e w ∈ R, so G is differentiable at e w. Hence G̃ is differentiable at w (composition with the differentiable linear map e), and DG̃(w) = DG(e w) ∘ e is injective as a composition of injective maps.
- G̃ is injective on F: if w, w′ ∈ F and G(e w) = G(e w′), injectivity of G on R gives e w = e w′, and injectivity of e gives w = w′.

4. (Image.) e is surjective, so e(e⁻¹(R)) = R and G̃(F) = G(e(e⁻¹(R))) = G(R) (Set.image_comp, Set.image_preimage_eq).

5. (Area formula.) Apply the sibling gram_area with m = 2, map G̃, Borel set F and integrand h; its hypotheses are step 3. Together with step 4 this gives
∫_{G(R)} h dμHE[2] = ∫_{G̃(F)} h dμHE[2] = ∫_F (det M(w))^{1/2} · h(G̃ w) dw,
where M(w) is the 2×2 matrix with entries M(w)_{ij} = ⟨DG̃(w)e_i, DG̃(w)e_j⟩ and dw is volume on E₂.

6. (Gram determinant of two vectors.) Fix w ∈ E₂ and put q := e w, a := DG(q)(1, 0), b := DG(q)(0, 1).
- By steps 3 and 1, DG̃(w)e₀ = DG(q)(e e₀) = a and DG̃(w)e₁ = DG(q)(e e₁) = b.
- Hence det M(w) = M₀₀M₁₁ − M₀₁M₁₀ = ⟨a, a⟩⟨b, b⟩ − ⟨a, b⟩⟨b, a⟩ = ‖a‖²‖b‖² − ⟨a, b⟩² (Matrix.det_fin_two, ⟨x, x⟩ = ‖x‖², symmetry of the real inner product).
- Also G̃ w = G q.
So for every w ∈ E₂ the integrand of step 5 equals Ψ(e w), where
Ψ(q) := (‖DG(q)(1, 0)‖²‖DG(q)(0, 1)‖² − ⟨DG(q)(1, 0), DG(q)(0, 1)⟩²)^{1/2} · h(G q).

7. (Back to ℝ × ℝ.) Since e is measure preserving and a measurable embedding, MeasurePreserving.setIntegral_preimage_emb gives ∫_{e⁻¹(R)} Ψ(e w) dw = ∫_R Ψ(q) dq. Combining steps 5–7, ∫_{G(R)} h dμHE[2] = ∫_R Ψ(q) dq, which is the claim. Every step is an equality of Bochner integrals: integrands were rewritten pointwise and the measure was transported, so no integrability hypothesis is needed. ∎

Formalization notes. A complete Lean proof of this exact type, using only the sibling Submission.codim1_lur_cd_injective_area_formula_gram and the frozen import closure, compiles.
- let e : Euclid 2 ≃L[ℝ] ℝ × ℝ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin 2) ℝ).trans (ContinuousLinearEquiv.finTwoArrow ℝ ℝ), with he : ∀ w, e w = (w 0, w 1) := fun w => rfl.
- hmp : MeasurePreserving e volume volume := (volume_preserving_finTwoArrow ℝ).comp (EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp (Fin 2)).
- hemb : MeasurableEmbedding e := e.toHomeomorph.measurableEmbedding.
- Measurability of e ⁻¹' R: e.continuous.measurable hR.
- hfd : ∀ w, fderiv ℝ (G ∘ e) w = (fderiv ℝ G (e w)).comp (e : Euclid 2 →L[ℝ] ℝ × ℝ) := fun w => e.comp_right_fderiv.
- Image: rw [Set.image_comp, Set.image_preimage_eq R e.surjective].
- Apply the sibling to P 2 (G ∘ e) (e ⁻¹' R), with:
  differentiability (hG (e w) hw).comp w e.differentiableAt;
  injectivity (by rw [hfd]; exact (hreg (e w) hw).comp e.injective);
  InjOn e.injective (hinj hw hw' heq).
- Integrand: e (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) = (1, 0) and e (EuclideanSpace.single 1 1) = (0, 1), each by rw [he]; simp. Then simp only [hfd, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply, ContinuousLinearEquiv.coe_coe, Matrix.det_fin_two, Matrix.of_apply, Function.comp_apply, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, real_inner_comm (fderiv ℝ G (e w) (1, 0))] followed by ring_nf.
- Finish: simp_rw the pointwise identity, then hmp.setIntegral_preimage_emb hemb Ψ R. Give Ψ explicitly; an underscore leaves a stuck NormedSpace instance.
proof_key_steps: e : Euclid 2 ≃L[ℝ] ℝ × ℝ, e w = (w 0, w 1), is a volume-preserving measurable embedding (volume_preserving_finTwoArrow composed with EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp).
G̃ = G ∘ e on F = e⁻¹(R): G̃ is differentiable, DG̃(w) = DG(e w) ∘ e is injective, G̃ is injective on F, and G̃(F) = G(R) because e is surjective.
Sibling gram_area with m = 2: ∫_{G(R)} h dμHE[2] = ∫_F √det[⟨DG̃(w)e_i, DG̃(w)e_j⟩] · h(G̃ w) dw.
DG̃(w)e₀ = DG(e w)(1, 0) and DG̃(w)e₁ = DG(e w)(0, 1); det_fin_two gives ‖a‖²‖b‖² − ⟨a, b⟩², so the integrand is Ψ(e w).
